task: Reconstruct the as-adopted decision and any supported relation to the delivered explanation of vote.

public.text: On 19 July 2024, the Council unanimously adopted draft S/2024/557 as resolution 2744, with all 15 voting in favour.

public.source: S/RES/2744 paras. 1–3 and Annex I n. 1
public.text: The resolution replaced the 1730 delisting procedure and directed sanctions committees other than the 1267 Committee to revise their guidelines. It requested that the Secretary-General appoint a new Focal Point within three months, in consultation with the working group.

malta.text: Malta said the Focal Point would engage with petitioners and gather information from several sources for a report to assist sanctions committees in their deliberations and decisions.

a3plus.source: S/PV.9689 p. 5, Guyana for Algeria, Mozambique, Sierra Leone and Guyana
a3plus.text: Speaking for the African members and Guyana, Guyana said a time-bound review would have been useful and urged effective implementation of the text’s continuous review provision.

switzerland.text: Switzerland called the independent Ombudsperson mechanism for the 1267 regime an ideal model and welcomed the strengthened Focal Point as progress.

review.source: S/RES/2744 paras. 4–5 and Annex II para. 6(a)
review.text: The Council expressed its intention to review the Focal Point’s mandate and work continuously. It established a consensus-based working group whose functions include reviewing the Focal Point’s twice-yearly reports.

authority.source: S/RES/2744 Annex I paras. 7, 9–10 and n. 3
authority.text: Annex I assigns the Focal Point a confidential factual report without a recommendation. When a relevant State or committee member recommends that delisting proceed, the committee decides under its normal procedures.

authority.early_claim: The delegate says the Focal Point assembles information into a report for sanctions committees to use in their own deliberations and decisions.
authority.late_claim: The adopted provision says the Focal Point provides factual observations without a recommendation and the relevant sanctions committee retains authority to decide.
authority.text: Malta described the committee-based process that Annex I establishes. The Focal Point informs the committee’s decision and has no power to recommend a result.

review.early_claim: The delegates say a time-bound review of the Focal Point would have been useful and want the continuous review provision implemented.
review.late_claim: The Council expresses an intention to review the mandate and tasks of the Focal Point continuously rather than setting a deadline for that review.
review.text: The A3+ would have preferred a time-bound review. The adopted text expresses an intention to keep the Focal Point under continuous review.

authority-quoted.text: In this fictional alternative, Malta rejected the suggestion that the Focal Point should assemble a factual report for sanctions committees to use in their own decisions. It instead called for decisions by the Focal Point.

authority-reversal.text: In this fictional alternative, an earlier draft assigned a factual report without a recommendation. The adopted annex instead gives the Focal Point the power to recommend a result and decide delisting requests.

review-quoted.text: In this fictional alternative, Guyana quoted and rejected someone else's view that a time-bound review would have been useful. The group supports ongoing review only.

review-reversal.text: In this fictional alternative, the Council rejected a proposal to keep the Focal Point's mandate and functions under continuous review. It required one review by a specified deadline instead.
